dedupe_keys.name: highd drone dataset of naturalistic vehicle trajectories on german highways

description: The highD dataset holds naturalistic vehicle trajectories recorded by drone on German highways. Traffic was filmed from above at six locations, avoiding the occlusions of ground-based sensors, and each vehicle's trajectory, type, size and manoeuvres were extracted automatically with computer vision, typically to within ten centimetres. It covers more than 110,500 vehicles, 44,500 driven kilometres and 147 driven hours, with different traffic states including congestion, and it comes with pre-extracted surrounding vehicles, time headway and time-to-collision metrics and manoeuvres such as lane changes, plus Python scripts for parsing and visualisation. It was created by a team at the Institute for Automotive Engineering of RWTH Aachen University (Krajewski, Bock, Kloeker, Eckstein) and presented at IEEE ITSC 2018. Coverage is six highway sites in Germany. Access: free of charge for academic and non-commercial research after an application that is checked manually; commercial use goes through leveLXData. Caveats: sites are short highway sections, and access requires approval. It supports calibration and validation of car-following and lane-change models, agent-based traffic simulation and safety surrogate analysis, and complements the NGSIM trajectories catalogued here.
